ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The figure is a distribution map of average sea-level pressure near Antarctica in January. <image1> According to the figure, infer what weather system is at the dashed line L?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the distribution of average sea-level pressure near Antarctica in January. Near the southern tip of South America and the Antarctic Peninsula there is a low-pressure center labeled "low", with dense isobars around it and cyclonic curvature. The dashed line L is located near this low-pressure center, and in form looks like a frontal line extending from one side of the low-pressure center. Then reason: Near the low-pressure center of an extratropical cyclone, there is often a frontal system. A warm front is usually located in front of or on one side of the low-pressure center, while a cold front is mostly dragged backward from the low-pressure center. The position and trend of dashed line L in the figure better conform to the characteristics of a warm front in the front part of the low pressure, so the dashed line L should be a warm front.
